VR is the future imo. In some form or another. People are "doom and gloom" about it at the moment because it's been out for a couple years and this is the first generation. That's typical adoption worries.

VR sales for both the PC VR headsets are over 500,000 based on Steam Hardware Survey. However, Sony's VR headset sold over 2 million units and was out for only a few months. The Vive sold 40,000 units in a few weeks in October of last year. Their total sold units is probably in the 300K range atm. Using that as a basis, along with steam hardware survey numbers for ratios of Vive to Rift, Rift probably has sold 200K

People want VR. The PC VR headsets have a lot of requirements like a good gaming PC to use them, so it makes sense that they would be far less because the cost is much higher.

Putting that into perspective, saying 500,000 PC VR headsets were sold and that they cost $600 each, that's a market worth $300 million. The Sony VR headset is $400 so that times 2 million is $800 million. A market worth over a billion dollars and it's only the first generation, within a year, roughly.

The biggest issues facing VR, imo, in order are:

  1. Few, if any, good VR games. I'm hoping Valve producing quality games will change this by giving the industry examples of "what is good to do" because Valve games tend to be fun, and by that metric, good games.
  2. Nausea. This will be fixed in software as developers find better ways to handle it. It's essentially a bug in an alpha product. It will go away eventually.
  3. Price. This will be fixed as new processes and mass production comes into play to drive the prices down on the hardware. We're already pushing more pixels than we need in most games. Hardware will get better and the headsets will improve. That's just another time thing.

The content is the real killer. I have friends who have the Vive, and that's their issue. The content isn't worth setting the Vive up. Some are considering selling it because they guess VR will be ready in like 3-5 years (as in, worthwhile to have), so they'll just buy a cheaper or just as expensive but better headset when that happens.

Overall, I'm excited for it, but it's early to want VR. This is a chicken or egg problem however, as content is the main killer and that has to come first since the headsets are already starting to come out. So Valve is betting on VR, and I'm glad they are doing so.

Besides, I'd expect these games to be playable without VR as well, but a much less enjoyable experience without it.
